chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The punishment for the grave-digger (who steals from a grave) is the same as the punishment for the thief.

key_terms.النَّبَّاشِ: The grave-digger or one who digs up graves to steal
key_terms.حَدّ: Fixed legal punishment prescribed in Sharia

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic punishment for stealing from a grave?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that grave robbers (*nabish*) receive the same *hadd* punishment as thieves (*sariq*), typically amputation of the hand. This equivalence underscores the sanctity of the grave in Shia jurisprudence, treating the removal of burial goods as a violation of property rights comparable to standard theft.
